verified: JEDEC published a preview of the DDR6 standard stating an initial RDIMM data rate of 12.8 GT/s, a 96-bit data bus split into four 24-bit sub-channels, 64 banks, 128 Gb (16 GB) dies and a pseudo-channel architecture, with modules 74 mm long versus 133 mm for DDR5, JEDEC's press release and Tom's Hardware report. Tom's Hardware's arithmetic puts baseline per-module bandwidth at 153.6 GB/s against DDR5's 38.4 GB/s.
unconfirmed: pin count, nominal voltage, burst length and supported form factors, which JEDEC has not disclosed and the report marks with question marks; the 4X figure is a baseline-versus-baseline comparison, only a little over 2X against DDR5-9200 RDIMMs (73.6 GB/s); module capacities of 128–256 GB consumer and up to 1 TB per server slot are the report's projections, not JEDEC figures; and no launch date exists — the 2029 commercialization target is third-party expectation, with no silicon, pricing or independent measurement reported.

verified: JEDEC 发布了 DDR6 的早期预览，拟定的服务器 RDIMM 起始速率为 12.8 GT/s，数据总线为 96 位，模块长度为 74 毫米；JEDEC 表示该标准仍在开发中，计划采用伪通道架构（pseudo-channel），以提升每个 DRAM 封装的带宽。
unconfirmed: 最终引脚数、工作电压、突发长度、正式形态与消费级首发速率均未公布；每插槽 1TB、2029 年商用只是规划或业界预期，4 倍带宽也是相对 DDR5 基线的换算而非实测（相对 DDR5-9200 峰值约 2.1 倍），JEDEC 未给出发布日期，也没有独立测试或量产样品验证。
